title: Polynomial & Rational Equations
summary: Higher-degree polynomial equations solve by factoring to zero-product form. Rational equations clear denominators by multiplying by the LCD, then solve — but you must reject any solution that makes an original denominator zero (extraneous).

polynomial equation.plain: A polynomial set equal to zero.
polynomial equation.in_class: Degree $n$ can have up to $n$ real roots.

zero-product property.plain: A product is 0 iff a factor is 0.
zero-product property.in_class: Solve each factor after full factoring.

LCD (equations).plain: Least common denominator to multiply through by.
LCD (equations).in_class: Removes all fractions from the equation.

extraneous solution.plain: A candidate that fails in the original equation.
extraneous solution.in_class: Usually makes a denominator zero — reject it.

factor completely.plain: Reduce a polynomial to prime factors.

degree and roots.plain: A degree-$n$ polynomial has $\le n$ roots.

check solutions.plain: Verify each candidate in the original.

concept_sections.heading: Higher-degree by factoring
concept_sections.explanation: Set the polynomial to zero, factor completely (GCF, grouping, special forms), and apply the zero-product property to each factor.

concept_sections.heading: Equations reducible to quadratic
concept_sections.explanation: Some equations become quadratic with a substitution (e.g. $u=x^2$ in $x^4-5x^2+4=0$). Solve for $u$, then back-substitute.
math_steps: Spot the quadratic pattern in a new variable.

concept_sections.heading: Clearing rational equations
concept_sections.explanation: Multiply every term by the LCD to remove denominators, turning the equation into a polynomial one you can solve.
math_steps: Find the LCD of all denominators.

concept_sections.heading: Extraneous solutions
concept_sections.explanation: Multiplying by the LCD can introduce false solutions. Check each candidate in the original: reject any that makes a denominator zero.
math_steps: Discard candidates equal to an excluded value.

concept_sections.heading: Verifying and counting
concept_sections.explanation: A degree-$n$ polynomial has at most $n$ real roots. Verify solutions and note repeated roots (multiplicity) where the graph touches without crossing.

real_world_examples.title: Concentration reaching a target
real_world_examples.scenario: Mixing to hit a desired strength.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The balance equation is rational; clearing denominators solves for the amount to add.

real_world_examples.title: Shared task time
real_world_examples.scenario: Two pumps drain a tank together.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: $\tfrac1a+\tfrac1b=\tfrac1t$ is a rational equation solved for the combined time.

real_world_examples.title: Designing a box
real_world_examples.scenario: Volume as a cubic in one dimension.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Setting the volume polynomial to a target and factoring gives the dimension.
